pages.title: Project Overview
pages.purpose: High-level introduction to cjquant: its purpose as a Chinese OTC fund quantitative framework, the four functional pillars, key design philosophy (share-NAV-liquidity timeline model), and how the library and web terminal relate. Links to all major child sections.

pages.title: Architecture and Module Map
pages.purpose: Describes the overall system architecture: the cjquant library package structure (backtest, data, optimizer, look_through, execution, visualizer), the FastAPI web app layer, and how they interconnect. Covers the quantitative workflow from data ingestion to execution.

pages.title: Getting Started and Installation
pages.purpose: Covers installation via pyproject.toml, Python version requirements, key dependencies (pandas, numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, akshare, plotly), running the web terminal (uvicorn / run_gui.py), and the desktop GUI launcher.

pages.title: Data Layer
pages.purpose: Overview of the data pipeline: how heterogeneous OTC fund data is fetched, normalized, aligned, and validated. Links to child pages covering providers, alignment, and schema.

pages.title: DataPipeline and Providers
pages.purpose: Details the DataPipeline facade class, PublicFundProvider (akshare/Eastmoney integration, retry logic, NAV fetching), PrivateFundLocalProvider (local CSV ingestion), and the BaseProvider interface. Covers the data_api singleton.

pages.title: Data Alignment and Schema
pages.purpose: Explains the DataAligner class and its three interpolation strategies (ffill, linear, proxy_mapping/Beta Mapping), the FundDataSchema validation contract (unit_nav, acc_nav, adj_nav columns), and error handling via DataFormatError and AlignmentError.

pages.title: Backtesting Engine
pages.purpose: Overview of the OTC backtesting system: its T+N settlement model, order lifecycle, and how it differs from exchange-based backtesting. Links to child pages for the engine, portfolio accounting, fee/slippage models, and data models.

pages.title: OTCBacktestEngine
pages.purpose: Deep dive into the OTCBacktestEngine class: initialization parameters (market_data, initial_cash, t_plus_confirm, t_plus_settle, slippage_model), the step() simulation loop, order submission, NAV cache, holiday handling, daily mark-to-market valuation, run_all(), and CSV export methods.

pages.title: Portfolio Accounting: TransitCashAccount and FundPosition
pages.purpose: Covers the three-stage cash lifecycle (available, frozen, transit), the TransitCashAccount class (lock_cash, add_to_transit, process_daily_arrival), FundPosition with FIFO lot-based accounting (PositionLot, process_sell), and floating-point epsilon tolerance.

pages.title: Fee Models, Slippage, and Data Models
pages.purpose: Explains OTCFeeModel tiered redemption fees (holding natural days, punitive rates), the slippage hierarchy (BaseSlippage, ZeroSlippage, SquareRootSlippage, CustomLambdaSlippage), the Order/TradeRecord/PositionLot dataclasses, and trade exceptions (InsufficientCashError, InsufficientPositionError).

pages.title: Portfolio Optimization
pages.purpose: Overview of the optimizer module: the BaseOptimizer contract, the four optimizer implementations, and the Ledoit-Wolf covariance shrinkage utility. Links to child pages for traditional and ML-based optimizers.

pages.title: Traditional Optimizers: Risk Parity and Mean-Variance
pages.purpose: Details RiskParityOptimizer (SLSQP, marginal risk contribution, equal risk contribution objective), MeanVarianceOptimizer (Sharpe ratio maximization, 252-day annualization, 2% risk-free rate), BaseOptimizer interface, and the calculate_shrunk_covariance utility (Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage).

pages.title: HRP and Black-Litterman Optimizers
pages.purpose: Covers HRPOptimizer (distance matrix, single-linkage clustering, quasi-diagonalization, recursive bisection — no matrix inversion required), and BlackLittermanOptimizer (prior equilibrium returns, views Q/P/Omega, Idzorek simplification, posterior expected return formula).

pages.title: Look-Through Analysis
pages.purpose: Overview of the look_through module: its purpose for decomposing fund portfolios into underlying factor/sector exposures, the two analysis methods, and the standardized ExposureResult output. Links to child pages for HBA and RBSA.

pages.title: LookThroughAnalyzer Facade and ExposureResult
pages.purpose: Describes the LookThroughAnalyzer factory/facade class (method selection: HBA vs RBSA, run() interface), the ExposureResult dataclass (fund_code, analysis_date, method, exposures dict, r_squared), and how downstream code consumes results uniformly.

pages.title: HBA Engine and RBSA Engine
pages.purpose: Details HBAEngine (HBASymbolResolver, holdings DataFrame schema, weight normalization, groupby aggregation for industry/style), and RBSAEngine (Sharpe's method, SLSQP optimization, sum-to-one and long-only constraints, R-squared calculation, rolling window support).

pages.title: Execution Layer
pages.purpose: Overview of the execution module: how internal orders are translated into institutional trade files. Links to child pages for the OTCExecutor API and O32 integration.

pages.title: OTCExecutor API
pages.purpose: Covers the OTCExecutor high-level API (buy/sell/clear/execute methods), order accumulation pattern, multi-channel dispatch (o32 and wechat), WeChat LiCaiTong CSV export (UTF-8-SIG encoding), and the output_dir/strip_suffix configuration.

pages.title: O32OrderExporter and Hundsun Integration
pages.purpose: Details O32OrderExporter: from_orders() vs from_trades() dispatch, direction mapping (BUY→申购, SELL→赎回), column renaming to Chinese O32 headers (证券代码, 业务类别, 组合编号, 资产单元), GBK encoding for Windows compatibility, and Excel export support.

pages.title: Visualization and Reporting
pages.purpose: Overview of the visualizer module: post-backtest performance analysis, metric calculation, and multi-format report generation. Links to child pages for metrics and plotting.

pages.title: CJQuantReporter and Report Generation
pages.purpose: Covers CJQuantReporter (stats_csv + trades_csv ingestion, generate_html/generate_png/generate_pdf methods), the HTML template with embedded Plotly, img2pdf soft dependency, and Chinese font configuration (SimHei) for Matplotlib.

pages.title: QualityMetrics and ReportPlotter
pages.purpose: Details QualityMetrics (Sharpe, Sortino, Calmar, Max Drawdown calculations, 252-day annualization, 2% risk-free rate), ReportPlotter interactive Plotly subplots (NAV, drawdown, asset composition stacked area, daily returns), and static Matplotlib summary (monthly return heatmap, turnover bar chart).

pages.title: Web Terminal and Application Layer
pages.purpose: Overview of the FastAPI web terminal (app/): its role as the integration layer between the cjquant library and the browser-based UI, the desktop GUI wrapper, and the strategy scheduler. Links to child pages.

pages.title: FastAPI Backend (app/main.py)
pages.purpose: Covers all REST API endpoints: strategy management (GET/PUT/POST /api/strategies), task scheduler (GET/POST /api/tasks, toggle, run, logs), portfolio operations (GET /api/portfolio, update, refresh_navs), analytics endpoints (optimize, correlation, performance, look_through, backtest), the BacktestContext proxy class, and the data fallback mechanism with simulated returns.

pages.title: Strategy Scheduler and Closed-Loop Portfolio Sync
pages.purpose: Explains the scheduler_loop async background task, tasks.json schema (name, strategy_file, schedule_type, schedule_value, enabled, status, last_run), subprocess isolation via asyncio.create_subprocess_exec, log streaming, and the sync_exported_orders_to_portfolio file-watch mechanism for O32 and WeChat CSV ingestion.

pages.title: Frontend UI: HTML, JavaScript, and CSS
pages.purpose: Covers the SPA architecture (tab-based navigation), app.js polling and state management (portfolioPollingInterval, logPollingInterval), the custom SVG backtest chart (drawBacktestChart), the Research Fund Pool reactive pattern (renderResearchFundPool), the correlation heatmap renderer, and the QMT-style CSS design system (flat/square aesthetic, Chinese A-share color conventions).

pages.title: Desktop GUI Launcher
pages.purpose: Describes run_gui.py and app/gui.py: the pywebview-based desktop wrapper, port detection (is_port_open), uvicorn subprocess management, health-check retry loop, graceful shutdown with terminate/kill fallback, and the 1366x850 window configuration.

pages.title: Example Strategies
pages.purpose: Overview of the bundled strategy scripts in app/strategies/: their role as runnable entrypoints and templates for users. Links to child pages for each strategy.

pages.title: Risk Parity Rebalance and Look-Through Monitor
pages.purpose: Details risk_parity_rebalance.py (run_strategy pipeline: data prep → RiskParityOptimizer → OTCExecutor → o32/wechat export) and otc_look_through_monitor.py (run_monitor pipeline: holdings ingestion → LookThroughAnalyzer HBA → threshold compliance check). Covers sys.path injection pattern.

pages.title: Backtest Demo and Custom Strategy Template
pages.purpose: Covers backtest_demo.py as a reference implementation for the init(context)/handle_bar(context) strategy interface used by the BacktestContext proxy in app/main.py, and the 永久投资组合.py (Permanent Portfolio) strategy as an example of a buy-and-hold allocation.
